discovered-from:SA-0MV9JVLBQ0090RNC

## Problem

The audit merge gate (`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` → `_resolve_item_integration_evidence`) mines every hex token from the work item's description and comments and keeps those that resolve to **any** git object in the owning repo (`_commit_object_exists`). It does not filter by which ref the commit is reachable from.

When an item's text cites commits that exist only on `refs/worklog/data`, its backup refs, or other non-`dev` refs (e.g. a worklog history-rewrite item quoting incident-era SHAs), `_verify_merged_in_dev` finds no ancestor of `origin/dev` among the candidates and the gate proceeds to `_integrate_into_dev`, which cherry-picks those commits onto a worktree at `origin/dev` — conflicting and failing the audit closed with a spurious `Ready to close: No` merge-gate blocker.

## Observed (2026-10-23, SA-0MV9JVLBQ0090RNC)

- Audit run 1: `git cherry-pick 345ea154a -> rc=1` conflict; verdict `Ready to close: No` (merge-gate blocker). `345ea154a` is a `refs/worklog/data` commit, never a `dev` commit.
- Workaround applied: the item description now records a real `dev` commit (`92fee5c30`, an ancestor of `origin/dev`), so the ancestor scan short-circuits to merged before any cherry-pick. Fragile — it depends on authors remembering to cite a `dev` commit and on the scan order.
- Related (already completed): SA-0MTQAF62U0085BEV (foreign hex that is not an object at all) and SA-0MTECRNGR000VKLV (decimal literals mined as SHAs). This is a third variant: the token **is** a commit object, but not on the delivery ref.

## Desired behaviour

- Restrict integration-evidence candidates to commits reachable from the item's delivery surface (branches matching `wl-<id>-*`, and any commit that is an ancestor of `origin/dev` or of a referenced feature branch) — or, at minimum, skip candidates not reachable from any `refs/heads/*` / `origin/*` ref of the owning repo, recording the skip as evidence.
- Commits reachable only from `refs/worklog/*`, `refs/backup/*` or unreachable objects must never be cherry-picked onto `dev`.
- Keep fail-open behaviour for evidence-less items and fail-closed behaviour for genuinely unmerged feature work.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1:** A work item whose description cites commits reachable only from `refs/worklog/data` (or a backup ref) does NOT trigger `_integrate_into_dev`; the gate records a skip note naming each excluded candidate and its non-delivery ref.
2. **AC2:** Regression test (in `skill/audit/tests/`) builds a fixture repo with a `dev` branch, a `refs/worklog/data` commit and a description citing that commit, and asserts `_phase_merge_gate` passes without invoking cherry-pick (no stray worktree, no blocker).
3. **AC3:** Existing behaviour is unchanged for: the real delivered commit (ancestor of `origin/dev` → merged), genuinely unmerged feature-branch work (still integrates), and evidence-less items (fail-open).
data.title: Audit merge gate treats commits on other refs (worklog/backup) as dev integration evidence

data.description:
# Finish gate: test the tree the commit produces, and prove every verdict's provenance

## Objective

Make `implement.py finish`'s test gate validate the exact tree the commit
will produce, and make every gate verdict self-describing (which tree ran,
whether it came from cache). A green gate must never again be produced by a
suite run against a different tree or by a stale cached result.

## Problem statement

`phase_finish` runs the test gate **before** it stages and commits
(`git_commit` performs `git add -A` afterwards). Suite tests that key off the
**tracked** file set (`git ls-files`) therefore cannot see files the commit is
about to add, and the gate can report a green full-scope run for a tree that
is red the moment the commit lands. The false green is silent: the report says
"full scope, success", so no agent looks further, and the tree stays red at
the push, in CI, and for the next agent.

Observed on ContentCreator work item **OSL-0MVK2F1Z300996SA** (Ep 1 of *Inside
the Content Creation Suite*):

- `implement.py finish` reported `{"tooling": "suite", "scope": "full",
  "success": true}` and pushed commit `9c88625c`.
- A full-suite run on the same tree immediately after reported **2 failed**,
  both caused by the newly added files:
  - `test_no_podcast_episode_content_tracked_outside_documented_leftovers` —
    `podcasts/ep1-why-use-it/*` were not yet in `git ls-files`, so the
    allowlist guard passed pre-commit and failed post-commit.
  - `test_registry_documents_match_on_disk_documents` — the wiki registry was
    stale for the new synthesis page. This test reads **on-disk** files, not
    `git ls-files`, so untracked-invisibility cannot explain its false pass.
- The item was re-finished (`9f3a1f6c`) after fixing the allowlist and
  rebuilding the metadata; the suite was green at that commit
  (`2765 passed, 16 skipped`). The defect is the false green, not the fix.

Origin record: **OSL-0MVKT9LN10097FA2** (ContentCreator worklog) — full intake
brief, investigation trail, and evidence.

## Investigation findings (from the origin intake)

Two mechanisms are supported; both must be closed:

1. **Untracked-file invisibility (proved).** `git_commit` stages *after* the
   test step, and the suite runs against the loose working tree. Anything
   using `git ls-files` semantics cannot see the commit's new files.
2. **Verdict may not correspond to a suite run at the gate's tree (root
   cause to pin).** Surviving cache evidence: the nearest green full-suite
   entry in the shared `.worklog/cache` (08:53, state `8e9c3ea7…`) collected
   **2751** tests, i.e. the dev tree before the episode work's test files
   existed; the post-commit red run (10:56, `f73d063e…`) collected **2781**,
   matching the committed tree. The gate's own per-worktree cache was deleted
   with the worktree, so the exact entry served cannot be recovered. Because
   the parity test reads disk, untracked-invisibility alone cannot explain its
   pass: the gate either executed against a different checkout/state or served
   a cached result recorded for a different tree.

## Desired change

1. **Temporary-index gate (operator-approved option A).** Before the gate's
   test step: copy the real index to a temp file, apply the change set to the
   copy (`GIT_INDEX_FILE=<tmp> git add -A`), and run the suite with
   `GIT_INDEX_FILE` exported so every child `git` command (including
   `git ls-files` inside tests) sees the staged file set. On success the real
   index receives `git add -A` and the commit proceeds; on failure the temp
   index is deleted and the real index and working tree are untouched.
   `GIT_INDEX_FILE` is currently **not** in `REPOSITORY_OVERRIDE_ENV_VARS`
   (`skill/shared/git_sandbox.py`), so it survives the runner's env scrub —
   this must be asserted by a regression test so a future scrub addition
   cannot silently break the fix.
2. **Verifiable verdicts.** The gate's report must state (a) the tree the
   suite ran against (worktree path + git fingerprint) and (b) whether the
   result was served from the cache. A cached verdict is acceptable only when
   its fingerprint is the would-be-commit tree's fingerprint; otherwise the
   suite must run.

Rejected: stage-then-test with unstage-on-abort (mutates the real index,
fragile restore); `git status --porcelain`-clean assertion only (demands a
clean tree and still does not test the commit's file set).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **Gate tests the would-be commit tree:** a change set that adds a file rejected by a tracked-file guard (`git ls-files` semantics) fails the finish gate, with the failing test named, instead of reporting a green full-scope pass. Reproduced through the finish-gate entry point.
- [ ] **The gate proves its verdict:** the report records the tree it ran against (worktree path + fingerprint) and whether the result came from cache; no green verdict is accepted for a state whose suite has not run (stale/foreign cache entries must miss).
- [ ] **Abort leaves the tree unchanged:** on gate failure there is no partial commit, no residual staging, and the temporary index is removed.
- [ ] **Cache determinism:** `GIT_INDEX_FILE` passes through the test skill's env scrub into child git commands (regression test), and the gate's cache key reflects the would-be-commit tree, not the loose working tree.
- [ ] **Existing green runs unaffected:** a clean change set passes exactly as today with a single gate suite execution (no duplicate run).
- [ ] **Parity false pass explained:** the regression work reproduces the disk-reading parity case at the finish-gate entry point and records the root cause (wrong checkout / stale cache / metadata lag before staging) in this work item.
- [ ] **Testing/validation:** the framework suites pass — `skill/implement/tests/`, `skill/test/tests/`, `tests/test_test_cache.py`, plus the repository full suite at the dev-push gate.
- [ ] **Documentation:** `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` (finish gate semantics, verdict provenance), `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` (cache fingerprint / `GIT_INDEX_FILE` contract) updated. CHANGELOG.md is managed by the ship skill and excluded.
## Constraints

- ✗ Do not weaken the gate: no default bypasses (`TEST_SCOPE_SKIP` etc.);
  guard ownership (`LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE`) and the nested-run stand-down
  contract stay intact.
- ✗ One suite execution per gate verdict on a clean change set.
- ✗ The changed-scope development gate stays the fast path; the full suite
  stays the dev-push integration gate.
- ✗ Implemented in this repository (framework); do not edit the global install
  directly.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_finish` test step,
  `git_commit`, `_run_resolved_suite` / `_run_guarded_suite`, gate report keys.
- `skill/test_cache.py` — `compute_git_state` / `run_cached` / `cache_dir`.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `guarded_run_all`, env construction
  (`subprocess_env_with_scrubbed_overrides`).
- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` — `REPOSITORY_OVERRIDE_ENV_VARS`.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_implement_guard_ownership.py`,
  `skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_scope.py`, `tests/test_test_cache.py` —
  regression-test homes.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** a temporary index changes *staged* status, which may surprise
  tests asserting on working-tree state beyond `git ls-files` (e.g.
  `git ls-files --error-unmatch` in ContentCreator's
  `test_implement_state_gitignore.py`). Mitigation: re-verify such tests in
  the regression work and document the semantics.
- **Risk:** two cache entries per state (loose vs staged fingerprint);
  accepted — correctness over hit ratio.
- **Assumption:** the parity false pass shares the gate-to-tree mismatch
  cause rather than a metadata-lag-only cause; the reproduction settles it.
- **Cross-repo note:** project-level fallout (ContentCreator's missing
  pre-push full-suite gate) is tracked separately in the OSL worklog, not
  here.

## Related work

- **OSL-0MVKT9LN10097FA2** — origin record and intake brief (ContentCreator).
- **OSL-0MVK2F1Z300996SA** — work item whose first finish produced the false
  green (`9c88625c`, corrected by `9f3a1f6c`).
- **SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81** — full suite deferred from finish to the dev-push gate.
- **SA-0MUIJAHXS003M7BG** — live-repo guard vs pre-push gate duration and
  implement push timeout.
- **SA-0MUG30J5F001L57H**, **SA-0MUH1MJL6003767Q** — guard ownership.
- **OSL-0MUHNOJ8E002YKUO** — accidental `.implement_state.json` tracking via
  the same `git add -A` staging surface.
data.title: Finish gate: test the tree the commit produces, and prove every verdict's provenance

Discovered-from: SA-0MVE34D9B005TUYJ (claim-hold fix).

## Problem
acquireFileLock() (~/projects/ContextHub/src/file-lock.ts) removes a lock whose acquiredAt is older than DEFAULT_MAX_LOCK_AGE_MS (5 min) even when the holder PID is alive on the same host. A long wl sync (fetch/merge/push over a slow network or a large store) therefore has its lock stolen mid-operation, and two writers proceed concurrently: the sync then writes back its pre-operation snapshot over whatever the stealer committed (the general lost-update class that WL-0MUV2U9QF002S9J1 closed for short operations).

## Why it was not fixed in SA-0MVE34D9B005TUYJ
The claim-hold guard now prevents the user-visible damage (a reverted claim), but non-claim field writes are still exposed in that window.

## Suggested direction
Treat a same-host live holder as authoritative (no age-expiry), keep age-expiry for dead-PID / foreign-host / unparseable locks, and/or refresh the lock (acquiredAt heartbeat) during long syncs. Add a deterministic regression test using the sync-vs-mutation.test.ts git-shim parking technique plus a back-dated lock file.

## Key Files
- ~/projects/ContextHub/src/file-lock.ts
- ~/projects/ContextHub/src/commands/sync.ts
- ~/projects/ContextHub/tests/cli/sync-vs-mutation.test.ts
data.title: wl sync: file-lock age-expiry steals a live holder's lock (residual lost-update hazard)

Discovered-from: SA-0MVE34D9B005TUYJ.

## Problem
run_tests.py --scope changed maps changed source files to tests via Python/.mjs conventions only (map_changed_to_tests / _is_test_file in skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py). For a vitest/TypeScript repo (ContextHub: tests/cli/**/*.test.ts, tests/unit/**/*.test.ts) a change to src/foo.ts or a new tests/cli/foo.test.ts selects nothing, so the gate silently falls back to the full suite (two npm test invocations, ~10+ minutes plus host slot contention).

## Why it matters
Fast changed-scope feedback is the implement skill's development-time gate; for the canonical wl repo (ContextHub) it degrades to the full suite every time, which also increases test-slot contention across concurrent agents.

## Suggested direction
Extend the convention mapping to TypeScript test files: <stem>.test.ts / <stem>.spec.ts in tests/{cli,unit}/ and any directory, plus a direct import-graph expansion (or a conservative 'same package directory' rule). Keep the existing fallback-to-full behaviour when nothing is selectable.

## Key Files
- skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py (map_changed_to_tests, _is_test_file, TRACKED_SOURCE_EXTENSIONS)
- tests/ for the runner's own coverage
## Extension (2026-10-29) — `suiteCommands` must not disable selection; honour declared `groups`

Cross-referenced from **MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6** (tce-main-street, high), which owns that work item's **AC2**. Producer decision **Q3 = A** on that item: *"Add a vitest/TS-aware selection and honour declared `groups` even when `suiteCommands` is present (`suiteCommands` defines the full suite only)."* This item is the SorraAgents home for that fix (extends, does not duplicate, `SA-0MUJKF2HP001BR51` — targeted test groups).

### Why the gap matters on tce-main-street

- `.pi/test-config.json` declares `suiteCommands` (3 commands) **and** 10 named `groups`. `changed_scope_commands()` returns `None` immediately when `suiteCommands` is present, so every `implement.py finish` warns `changed-scope selection unavailable … falling back to full scope`. Reproduced twice on a change set with one new test file and three modified files (`MS-0MVPY2YDQ000S0G6`).
- Even without that guard, `map_changed_to_tests()` maps only pytest and `*.test.mjs`, so a vitest `.test.ts` change selects nothing.
- Cost: a full suite measured **2846.6 s** on a loaded host versus `timeoutPerCommand: 1800`, so documentation- and evidence-only finishes time out for reasons unrelated to their change.

### Additional acceptance criteria for this item

- [ ] `changed_scope_commands()` no longer early-returns when `suiteCommands` is declared; `suiteCommands` continues to define **only** the full suite (`full_suite_commands`), never the changed-scope subset.
- [ ] A change set matching a declared `groups` entry's `paths` selects that group's `commands` and reports `scope: changed` with the selected commands.
- [ ] A change set containing a changed/new vitest `*.test.ts` (and, conservatively, `*.spec.ts`) file selects those files (convention mapping extended to TypeScript), reporting `scope: changed`.
- [ ] When no safe subset exists, the fallback reports the **specific** reason (e.g. "no changed source/test files", "no matching group") instead of the current generic list of causes.
- [ ] Proven by selector unit tests: vitest/TS mapping, `suiteCommands` present + `groups` match, `suiteCommands` present + no match → named fallback reason; plus a live `implement.py finish` log on tce-main-street showing `scope: changed` (recorded on `MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6`).
- [ ] The full-suite gate is unchanged: a green full-scope run is still required where the change set cannot be safely narrowed.

### Note for the producer

Priority left unchanged (`low`) because this session was not authorised to re-prioritise; **MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6 is `high` and depends on this item**, so raising it to `medium`/`high` is recommended when next triaged.
data.title: test skill: changed-scope mapper does not map vitest .test.ts files (ContextHub falls back to full suite)

## Goal

Once SA-0MVLJ8VD60091JLW makes `/proc/pressure` actually parse, the existing pressure thresholds need a calibration pass against real host data.

## Context

- `cpu_pressure` (70/85) is now applied to the `some` avg10 line — plausible, unvalidated.
- `io_pressure` (50/80) was chosen when the parser produced nothing and is applied to the `full` avg10 line; 50% full-stall is effectively never reached, so the metric would stay green under genuine I/O starvation.

## Acceptance criteria

- Thresholds for `cpu_pressure` and `io_pressure` are validated against observed stall percentages on a busy multi-agent host.
- `config.yaml` / `config.py::_DEFAULTS` / `SKILL.md` are updated consistently with the calibrated values and the rationale is recorded.
- Tests cover the new thresholds' classification boundaries.

## Notes

- discovered-from:SA-0MVLJ8VD60091JLW (scope-creep risk recorded there rather than widening that item).
- Related: ContextHub WL-0MVI8YM07002Z9VY (process/thread/swap threshold miscalibration).

Discovered while implementing SA-0MVHXWLPG007OQVN (drive timeout reconciliation).

Problem: when implement.py start runs from inside an already-existing worktree (the resume path used by every driven child session), Step 9 writes ImplementState.repo_root = str(Path.cwd().resolve()) — the worktree path, not the main checkout. phase_finish then calls _remove_worktree(worktree_path, repo_root=state.repo_root) whose safety gate 1 refuses when resolved_path == repo_root (CRITICAL: REFUSE to remove the repository root ... This is the main working tree, not a worktree; Restored status=open).

Impact: every driven child leaks its worktree, finish exits non-zero and restores the item to open even though the commit was pushed — a false failure needing manual status fix; .worklog/worktrees accumulates orphans.

Expected: phase_start should persist the main checkout root (e.g. via _main_checkout_for(worktree) following the gitdir) so phase_finish can remove the worktree after a successful push.

Evidence: SA-0MVLJWL60001H6QK finish (commit b11d0877d pushed to dev, finish reported failure, worktree left in place).
data.title: implement.py finish refuses to remove a resumed worktree because phase_start stores the worktree as repo_root

data.description:
Discovered by a full-project `/skill:refactor` scan of this repository (499 source files, clean `dev` checkout).

## User Story

**As a** producer running a refactor scan,
**I want** the report's "Auto-fixed" count to reflect changes actually written to disk,
**so that** I can trust the report and do not believe lint debt was cleaned when the tree is
byte-for-byte unchanged.

## Observed behaviour

`python3 skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py` (no work-item id) reported:

```
Auto-fix applied 9 fixes via linters on 437 files
Auto-fixed:     9
Remaining smells: 9
```

but `git status` showed **no** source-file changes (only a pre-existing modification to
`.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`), and a follow-up check confirmed the same 9 diagnostics
are still present:

```
$ ruff check --select SIM102,EXE005,ISC004,SIM115,UP031,SIM117,EXE001 \
    skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py skill/implement/scripts/implement.py \
    skill/shared/tests/test_wait_for_job.py skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_failure_notices.py \
    tests/test_author_gate_allowlist.py tests/test_background_job_etiquette_docs.py
Found 9 errors.
No fixes available (3 hidden fixes can be enabled with the `--unsafe-fixes` option).
```

The same 9 findings are then also listed under "Remaining smells (non-auto-fixable)", i.e. they are
counted twice: once as fixed, once as outstanding.

## Root cause (suspected)

`_parse_ruff_fix_output()` in `skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py` turns **every** JSON entry emitted by
`ruff check --fix --output-format json` into a "fixed finding". Ruff's JSON output after `--fix`
contains the diagnostics that **remain** (those it could not or would not fix, e.g. EXE005/EXE001
shebang/exec bit rules and unsafe-fix candidates), not a ledger of applied fixes. Findings with a
null `fix` field should not be counted as applied.

`_parse_eslint_fix_output()` should be checked for the same assumption.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `_parse_ruff_fix_output()` / `_parse_eslint_fix_output()` count a finding as fixed only when the
   linter actually applied a fix (e.g. ruff entry carries a non-null `fix` payload, or fixes are
   detected by comparing file content before/after the run).
2. A regression test proves that a linter run over files whose remaining diagnostics are
   non-fixable reports `fixes_applied: false` / `Auto-fixed: 0`.
3. A full-project scan of a clean tree leaves `git status` unchanged **and** reports `Auto-fixed: 0`.
4. The "Remaining smells" list is not a duplicate of the auto-fixed list for the same diagnostics.
data.title: Refactor skill reports unfixed linter diagnostics as applied auto-fixes

data.description:
## Goal

As the operator reading my daily standup, I want the "Yesterday I completed work on..." section to separate **auto-dispatched** work (the herdr downtime dispatcher ran `/skill:implement`, `/skill:plan`, `/skill:intake`, `/skill:audit`, `/skill:effort-and-risk` without me) from **manually dispatched** work (I asked an agent to do it in a session I started), so I can see how much of yesterday's progress was machine-driven versus operator-driven.

## Current behaviour

- `skill/standup/scripts/generate_standup.py` (`generate_report`, ~line 852) builds `yesterday_items` from `fetch_all_completions_in_window(window_start, window_end)` — every `completed`/`in_review` item whose `updatedAt` falls in the 24 h window, in one flat list.
- Both the markdown report and `yesterday_tts` render that flat list; `--json` exposes a single `yesterday` array.
- Nothing in the pipeline distinguishes provenance, so a `wl next`-selected item implemented by the downtime worker looks identical to one I personally kicked off.

## Provenance signal (already exists — do not invent a new one)

The herdr downtime worker already records provenance in two places:

1. **`.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`** — bounded JSONL (cap `DOWNTIME_LOG_MAX_ENTRIES = 100`, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts`). Each dispatch entry carries `itemId`, `kind` (`intake`|`plan`|`implement`|`audit`|`risk-effort`|`scheduled`), `dispatchedAt`, `cwd`, `title`, `stage`, and post-spawn enrichment fields (`paneId`, `outcome`). `downtime-coordination.log` and `local-route.log` are separate files and must NOT be treated as dispatch markers.
2. **Worklog comment marker** — `buildDowntimeDispatchComment()` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`, ~line 7951) writes: `Auto-dispatched by the herdr downtime worker at <ISO> — running <skill> <itemId> (<title>).` This survives the rolling-log trim.

Classification rule to implement: an item is **auto-dispatched** iff it has a matching live dispatch-log entry (`itemId`, and `outcome` is not `spawn-failed`) **or** a worklog comment containing the `Auto-dispatched by the herdr downtime worker at` prefix within/before the window; otherwise **manual**. Items with no detectable marker default to manual (fail-open to the smaller, less confusing bucket) and the default must be documented.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1: The markdown "Yesterday I completed work on..." section is split into two labelled sub-groups, auto-dispatched first then manual (or an explicitly documented order), each with a plain-language heading (TTS-friendly, e.g. "Work auto-dispatched by the downtime worker" and "Work I dispatched myself").

- [ ] AC2: Each sub-group is omitted when empty; the section never renders an empty heading. If the entire window is empty, the existing empty-section behaviour is preserved.

- [ ] AC3: `--json` exposes the split without breaking the existing contract: `yesterday_auto`, `yesterday_manual` (+ `_count` fields) are added and the existing `yesterday` / `yesterday_count` / `yesterday_tts` keys keep their current meaning (all items, unchanged ordering) so downstream consumers do not regress.

- [ ] AC4: TTS output (`yesterday_tts` renders) speaks the split in first person, e.g. "Yesterday the downtime worker completed..." / "I completed..."; no IDs, backticks, or ISO timestamps in spoken lines.

- [ ] AC5: Classification is unit-tested with fixtures — (a) item with a dispatch-log entry → auto, (b) item with only a worklog comment marker → auto, (c) `outcome: spawn-failed` entry → manual, (d) item with no marker → manual, (e) item in `downtime-coordination.log` / `local-route.log` only → manual, (f) trimmed/absent log file → falls back to comment markers and never raises.

- [ ] AC6: Read-side failures (missing/unreadable `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`, unparseable JSONL lines, `wl comment list` failure) degrade gracefully: the report still renders, the affected items land in the manual bucket, and a warning is logged — the exit code stays 0.

- [ ] AC7: `skill/standup/SKILL.md` documents the new section layout, the provenance rule, the default-to-manual behaviour, and the new `--json` fields.

- [ ] AC8: Existing standup tests (`skill/standup/tests/`) remain green; new tests are hermetic (`--no-sync --no-commit`, tmp worklog dirs, no real `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` reads).

## Out of scope

- Counting/dashboards of auto vs manual ratios (follow-up if wanted).
- Changing how the downtime dispatcher records markers.
- Re-ranking or filtering the Herdr selection list (WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2 rule stands: the Herdr list stays the sole ranking path; the split is presentational grouping only).

## Risks / notes

- The dispatch log is a **rolling 100-entry** log, so a busy day can trim entries within the 24 h window; the comment marker path is the durable fallback and both must be combined by OR.
- `kind: scheduled` entries are dispatcher-driven (scheduled prompts) and should be counted as auto-dispatch; document the decision.
- Grouping must not change item ordering inside a group (keep `updatedAt` then `id` sort) or `yesterday_count`.

# Framework pre-push hook v3 should resolve the global test runner

**Origin:** `discovered-from:OSL-0MVMCP5DT005PIFS` (filed from ContentCreator; that item was deleted once this one existed and was synced).

**Headline:** The framework's v3 pre-push hook refuses every `dev`/`main` push unless the pushed repo ships its own `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`, so `install_pi.sh` still ships a gate-less v2 hook to every project without one. Make v3 resolve the runner local-then-global (the pattern the same file already uses for the context-budget gate), ship v3 everywhere, and upgrade stale installed copies.

## Problem statement

Only the SorraAgents checkout contains `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`; every other project receives its skills from the global install at `~/.pi/agent/skills`. The v3 hook's full-suite gate looks for the runner at `$repo_root/skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` only, so in every non-SorraAgents repo the gate hard-fails (`exit 1`) on any push to `dev`/`main`. `scripts/install_pi.sh` works around that by installing `.githooks/pre-push.v2` — a hook **without** the full-suite gate — into every project that lacks a repo-local runner. The result is two hook variants, and the documented "a red tree is never pushed" guarantee is absent from every project except SorraAgents itself.

The cost is visible: `OSL-0MVL2OUW0003C6YX` had to hand-write a local-then-global runner lookup into ContentCreator's hook (its only deviation from the framework's) before the full-suite push gate could be restored there.

## Users

- **Agents pushing to `dev`** in any framework project — they need the same push-time guarantee everywhere, not only in SorraAgents.
- **The operator / producer** — one hook to audit, one documented contract, no per-repo fork to drift.
- **Project maintainers running `install_pi.sh`** — a fresh install must not choose a weaker hook, and a stale installed hook must not silently keep the weaker one.

Example user stories:

- As an agent pushing to `dev` in a project with no repo-local `skill/` tree, I want the full suite to run through the global runner, so a red tree is refused before it reaches the shared branch.
- As a maintainer, I want `install_pi.sh` to install one hook for every project, so I never have to reason about which variant my repo received.
- As the operator, I want an incomplete install to refuse the push and name the bypass, rather than silently skipping the gate.

## Desired change

1. **Runner resolution (v3 hook).** Resolve the runner local-then-global inside the full-suite gate, mirroring the context-budget block in the same file:
   - `$repo_root/skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` when present;
   - else `$HOME/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/run_tests.py`;
   - when neither exists, fail closed and name `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1` (unchanged fail-closed stance, better message).
   This makes the framework hook converge with the block ContentCreator already runs (`OSL-0MVL2OUW0003C6YX` AC2), so the project copy can eventually be deleted rather than forked.
2. **One hook variant.** `scripts/install_pi.sh` installs the v3 hook in every project — the `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` precondition is dropped and `.githooks/pre-push.v2` is removed (or reduced to a pointer note), with the hook-selection comments and `docs/dev/context-budget.md` corrected to describe reality.
3. **Installed-hook upgrade.** `install_pi.sh` must no longer leave a stale installed `.githooks/pre-push` in place forever: when the file's revision marker is a framework revision older than the current one **and the file is an unmodified framework copy**, replace it (backup the previous file, report what happened); when the file carries local modifications, report it and leave it alone. Re-running is idempotent (no rewrite when already current).
4. **Documentation.** The hook contract, the runner resolution order, the revision markers and the upgrade path are documented in the framework docs (`docs/dev/context-budget.md`, plus a hook section or `docs/dev/pre-push-hook.md` mirroring the project-side doc), and the hook header comment states the resolution order.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Global runner resolution:** with no repo-local `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` but a global `~/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/run_tests.py`, a `refs/heads/dev` push through the v3 hook executes the global runner with `--scope full --strict-git-env` from the pushed repo's root, and a green run permits the push (regression test, fake global runner).
- [ ] **Fail-closed unchanged:** with neither runner present, the hook exits non-zero on a `dev`/`main` push and names `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1`; feature-branch pushes and `refs/worklog/data` pushes still do not invoke the gate.
- [ ] **Parity with the project hook:** the framework gate block and ContentCreator's `.githooks/pre-push` gate block (`OSL-0MVL2OUW0003C6YX`) resolve the runner identically — same order, same fail-closed message semantics — asserted by a test that compares the two resolution behaviours (not the whole files, because the Worklog-sync ordering still differs).
- [ ] **One variant shipped:** `install_pi.sh` installs the v3 hook into a project with no repo-local runner (regression test in `tests/test_install_pi_hook_wiring.py`), and no install path can select a hook without the full-suite gate.
- [ ] **Installed-hook upgrade:** an existing `.githooks/pre-push` carrying an older framework revision marker and no local modifications is replaced (with a backup and a report); a locally modified hook is reported and left untouched; a second run changes nothing.
- [ ] **Upgrade safety:** upgrading a project that previously ran the v2 hook preserves its existing gate behaviour (branch policy, context budget, Worklog sync semantics) — the replaced hook is the framework v3 hook verbatim, and a test asserts the installed file's revision marker and gate blocks.
- [ ] **Testing/validation criterion:** full SorraAgents suite passes with the new tests, including `tests/test_pre_push_test_gate.py`, `tests/test_pre_push_hook_fallback.py`, `tests/test_install_pi_hook_wiring.py`, `tests/test_context_budget_rollout_docs.py`.
- [ ] **Documentation:** all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (`docs/dev/context-budget.md`, hook header, install script comments; the project-side `docs/dev/pre-push-hook.md` is referenced, not edited, since it lives in ContentCreator).
- [ ] **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- ✗ Do not weaken the gate: the missing-runner path stays fail-closed, `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1` stays the only bypass, `--scope full --strict-git-env` stays mandatory.
- ✗ Do not change branch-policy, context-budget or Worklog-sync semantics as a side effect of the runner fix.
- ✗ Do not overwrite a hook that carries local modifications (ContentCreator's copy deliberately keeps per-push Worklog sync — `OSL-0MVL2OUW0003C6YX` Q3); detect and report instead (see Q4).
- ✗ Framework code is edited in the SorraAgents repo, never from a project worktree.
- ✗ No ad-hoc test runs during implementation; use the test skill.

## Existing state

- `SorraAgents/.githooks/pre-push` (marker `worklog:pre-push-hook:v3`): branch policy → context-budget gate (local-then-global `measure_context.py`) → single stdin capture loop → full-suite gate (`runner="$repo_root/skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py"`, hard `exit 1` when absent) → feature-branch early exit → Worklog sync.
- `SorraAgents/.githooks/pre-push.v2`: same file without the full-suite gate and without the early exit (Worklog sync runs on every push).
- `scripts/install_pi.sh` (~lines 262–310): picks v3 only when `$CURRENT_REPO_ROOT/skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` exists, else copies `pre-push.v2`; copies only when `.githooks/pre-push` is absent, so an installed copy is never refreshed.
- `run_tests.py` resolves the project at CLI time via `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, so a global invocation is safe as long as cwd is the pushed repo (ContentCreator's hook proves this in production).
- Existing tests: `tests/test_pre_push_test_gate.py` (behavioural, fake local runner), `tests/test_pre_push_hook_fallback.py` (context-budget local-then-global resolution), `tests/test_install_pi_hook_wiring.py` (v2/v3 selection), `tests/test_context_budget_rollout_docs.py` (doc/hook comment assertions).
- ContentCreator's hook already implements the target resolution and failing-test reporting; it is the reference implementation, differing from framework v3 only in that deviation plus the retained per-push Worklog sync.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.githooks/pre-push` — full-suite gate: add local-then-global runner resolution mirroring the context-budget block; improve the missing-runner message; bump the revision marker.
- `.githooks/pre-push.v2` — remove (single-variant install), or convert to a deprecation note if a test depends on its presence.
- `scripts/install_pi.sh` — drop the runner precondition, always install v3, add the revision-marker upgrade step with backup and local-modification detection, update comments.
- `tests/test_pre_push_test_gate.py` — add global-runner and neither-runner cases (fake runner injected into a fake `$HOME`).
- `tests/test_pre_push_hook_fallback.py` — extend the existing fallback harness to the test runner (or add a sibling test module for it).
- `tests/test_install_pi_hook_wiring.py` — install-into-project-without-runner, upgrade-of-stale-copy, local-modification-preserved, idempotence.
- `docs/dev/context-budget.md` — hook contract and variant documentation corrected; runner resolution and upgrade path added.
- `docs/dev/pre-push-hook.md` (framework) — optional: the framework-side companion to ContentCreator's doc.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk (behaviour regression in ContentCreator):** a wholesale overwrite of an existing hook would drop ContentCreator's per-push Worklog sync (framework v3 exits early on feature pushes). Mitigation: overwrite only unmodified framework copies (Q4); report modified ones.
- **Risk (global runner resolves the wrong project):** the global `run_tests.py` resolves its repo from cwd; if the hook ran it from anywhere else, it would test the wrong tree. Mitigation: keep `cd "$repo_root"` (already the case in the project hook) and assert the cwd in the regression test.
- **Risk (install churn):** rewriting hooks on every install produces noisy diffs in every project. Mitigation: revision-marker comparison, no write when current.
- **Risk (scope creep):** ContentCreator's hook fork, the divergent `post-checkout`/`post-merge`/`post-rewrite` hooks, and the release pipeline are out of scope; record as linked items rather than folding them in.
- **Assumption:** this SA item carries the implementation; the `OSL-` origin record was deleted once this item existed and was synced (Q1).
- **Assumption (Q4):** "overwrite existing installed hooks" applies to unmodified framework copies only; locally modified hooks are reported, not clobbered.

## Related work

- `OSL-0MVL2OUW0003C6YX` — *Restore the full-suite pre-push gate in ContentCreator* (completed): the project-side fix whose comment filed this follow-up; its Q3 decision (keep per-push Worklog sync) constrains the overwrite.
- `SA-0MV8M4OVX000QHSM` — *install_pi.sh propagates the SorraAgents-only test gate to non-SorraAgents projects* (completed): introduced the v2/v3 split this item retires.
- `SA-0MUIJAHXS003M7BG` — pre-push gate duration vs `implement.py` push timeout (cold-cache cost of the gate).
- `SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81` — full suite deferred from finish to the dev-push gate.
- `OSL-0MVKT9LN10097FA2` — finish-gate false green that surfaced the missing push gate.
- `OSL-0MVK2F1Z300996SA` — the item whose `9c88625c` was pushed red.
- `OSL-0MTMS9R58000J613`, `OSL-0MT5Z8AJ7008LCQQ` — earlier pre-push hook defects (non-fatal `wl sync`, author-identity gate).
- `SA-0MUJLT3BH001IPWK` — active pre-push hook vs committed v3 wiring drift (same hook, adjacent defect).
- `SA-0MVB713300020UFB` — migrate pre-push hook fixtures to `git_sandbox` (touches the same test fixtures).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (ownership/location).** Where should the implementation and the tracked item live?
  - Options: (a) create a sibling `SA-` item in the SorraAgents store and delete this `OSL-` item as the origin record; (b) implement in SorraAgents but keep this `OSL-` item as the tracked item; (c) keep it ContentCreator-local.
  - **Recommended:** (a) — repository-boundary rule; matches `OSL-0MVKT9LN10097FA2` → `SA-0MVL2NH1G0094FA2`.
  - **Answer (operator, interactive reply):** **(a)** — "delete this item when the SA item is created and synced". Implementation: sibling `SA-` item created in the SorraAgents store; this `OSL-` item deleted after both stores sync.
- **Q2 (install_pi.sh scope).**
  - Options: (a) full unification — v3 for every project, drop `pre-push.v2`, overwrite existing installed hooks; (b) runner fallback only, leave the variant selection; (c) runner fallback + v3 for new installs, never overwrite, document a manual upgrade.
  - **Recommended:** (c) — overwriting risked clobbering ContentCreator's deliberate deviation.
  - **Answer (operator, interactive reply):** **(a)** — full unification, including overwriting existing installed hooks. Consequence recorded in Q4.
- **Q3 (missing-runner behaviour).**
  - Options: (a) fail closed naming `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1`; (b) fail open with a warning.
  - **Recommended:** (a) — the documented "a red tree is never pushed" guarantee must not vanish silently.
  - **Answer (operator, interactive reply):** **(a)**.
- **Q4 (derived from Q2 = a; flagged for producer confirmation).** Overwriting installed hooks conflicts with ContentCreator's deliberate deviation: its hook keeps per-push Worklog sync, while framework v3 exits early on feature-branch pushes (`OSL-0MVL2OUW0003C6YX` Q3), and `tests/test_pre_push_hook.py` there asserts sync on feature pushes. Two readings of "overwrite":
  - (i) overwrite unmodified framework copies only (revision marker matches a known framework revision and the file has no local edits); report and skip modified files — **no change to v3's Worklog-sync semantics**;
  - (ii) overwrite unconditionally — requires first changing v3 so feature-branch pushes still sync, i.e. deleting the early exit and updating `tests/test_pre_push_test_gate.py`.
  - **Recommended:** (i) — satisfies Q2 (stale framework copies are upgraded automatically) without changing documented framework hook semantics or breaking another repo's suite. **Status: assumption recorded in this brief; producer to confirm (ii) if unconditional overwrite is wanted.**

## Related work (automated report)

Generated by `find-related` (SA-0MVNUMMOA002LCB1); full untruncated report at
`.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-SA-0MVNUMMOA002LCB1.md`.

### Related work items

- **SA-0MUJLT3BH001IPWK** – Reconcile active pre-push hook with committed v3 (context-budget gate wiring drift) (open)
- **SA-0MVB713300020UFB** – Migrate pre-push hook fixtures to `git_sandbox` (blocked) — touches the same hook test fixtures
- **SA-0MR3P8N3V001Q3RG** – Add rebuild step to implement SKILL.md after git pull (completed) — unrelated, incidental match

> Repository file matches were generic-word noise (the hook's own tests and
> `audit_runner.py`); the curated **Key Files (predicted)** section is the
> useful list. The two open hook items are genuine neighbours, not duplicates.

# implement.py parent: terminal blockers still gate topological readiness

relocated-from:AH-0MVL5B7C80000MT6 (AI_Hell worklog), moved to this repo because `implement.py` is agent-infrastructure code owned by SorraAgents (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`).

discovered-from:AH-0MV8BUKFK003Z23S

## Problem statement

`implement.py parent` builds its dependency graph from **every** in-chain
dependency edge, including edges whose blocker is already terminal, so a
finished blocker still occupies the topological ordering and delays — or in
practice starves — the genuinely ready child that depends on it. A child whose
blockers are all terminal is *ready now*, yet it can be sorted behind unrelated
children purely because its (finished) blocker had a high `sortIndex`.

## Users

- **Primary — agent/operator running an epic:** "As the agent driving an epic
  with `implement.py parent`, I want a child whose blockers are all already
  finished to be selected as soon as it is the lowest-sorting ready child, so
  in-flight implementation work is never skipped and I never have to finish it
  manually."
- **Secondary — producer/reviewer:** "As a producer, I want the reported
  implementation order to mean 'blockers first, then sortIndex', so I can
  predict which child the next run will start."
- **Maintainer:** "As a maintainer, I want the ordering fix covered by a
  regression test with the exact shape that broke, so the readiness rule
  cannot silently regress."

## Observed failure (2026-10-23, epic AH-0MV8BUKFK003Z23S)

Resolved order for the epic's 8 children:

`[TOOK(test-failure, done), 3X5M, MVIS(done), VDA9, 7NGZ, O53Z(done), K0V4, BAAN]`

`K0V4` (sortIndex 3000 — the *lowest* open child) has an outbound `depends-on`
edge to `O53Z` (its test-first contract child, sortIndex 8100). `O53Z` was
already `completed`, so `K0V4` should have been ready immediately; instead it
was released only after `O53Z`'s slot near the end of the queue.

Consequences:

1. `implement.py parent AH-0MV8BUKFK003Z23S` never reached `K0V4` although its
   worktree held a completed in-flight implementation — it returned
   "start child VDA9"; the in-flight work had to be finished manually with
   `implement.py finish K0V4`.
2. The reported order is not "blockers first" in any intuitive sense: a ready
   child was deferred behind unrelated children purely because its finished
   blocker sorted late.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Terminal blockers never gate readiness.** In
   `_resolve_implementation_order()` an in-chain dependency edge whose blocker
   is terminal — `_is_terminal_child()` is true: status in `TERMINAL_STATUSES`
   (`in_review`, `completed`, `done`, `deleted`) or the item is soft-deleted —
   contributes neither to `in_degree[child]` nor to `dependents[blocker]`. The
   graph is therefore built over non-terminal children only, and a child whose
   in-chain blockers are all terminal is in the **initial** ready set.
2. **Ready children are ordered by their own `(sortIndex, id)`.** For the
   reproduction shape (open child `LOW` with sortIndex 3000 whose only in-chain
   blocker is a `completed` child `HIGH` with sortIndex 8100, plus an unrelated
   open child `MID` with sortIndex 5000) the resolved order starts with `LOW`,
   then `MID`, then `HIGH` — i.e. `LOW`'s position is decided by its own
   `sortIndex`, never by its blocker's.
3. **Regression test reproduces the exact shape.** A new
   `skill/implement/tests/test_resolve_implementation_order.py` covers at
   minimum: (a) the reproduction shape above, asserting `LOW` is **first**;
   (b) an all-terminal children set, asserting ordering is purely
   `(sortIndex, id)`; (c) a non-terminal chain `A ← B` (both open), asserting
   `A` precedes `B` (real blocking still respected); (d) a soft-deleted blocker
   treated as terminal; (e) an external blocker (id not among the children)
   creating no edge; (f) the existing cycle path still returning
   `([], error)` with the cyclic children named; (g) `_next_child_to_implement`
   still refusing a child whose in-chain blocker is **non**-terminal. The
   reproduction test must be shown red against the pre-fix source and green
   after the fix.
4. **No change to adjacent behaviour.** Cycle detection (fail-fast, no infinite
   recursion), cross-project/external-blocker reporting, `_classify_child`
   (`skip-terminal` / `skip-in-progress`) and the blocked-child guard in
   `_next_child_to_implement` are unchanged, and the parent still advances once
   every child is terminal.
5. **Documentation updated.** The
   `_resolve_implementation_order()` docstring states the readiness rule
   (terminal blockers are pre-satisfied), and the parent-recursion/dependency
   ordering text in `skill/implement/SKILL.md` (plus any `docs/dev/*` reference
   that describes the ordering) is updated to match; code comments explain why
   terminal edges are excluded.
6. **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes**, including
   code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes** — the
   implement-skill group (`pytest -q skill/implement/tests/`) is green and the
   full suite (`skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py --scope full`) passes on the
   committed tip.

## Constraints

- **Repository ownership.** The code is agent infrastructure owned by **SorraAgents**:
  `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (`~/.pi/agent/skills` is a symlink to
  `SorraAgents/skill`; the AI_Hell checkout contains no `skill/` tree). The item
  was relocated here from the AI_Hell worklog (AH-0MVL5B7C80000MT6) by producer
  decision, following the SA-0MUWNKUIU007N876 precedent, while keeping its
  `discovered-from` link to the AI_Hell epic that exposed the defect. The change,
  its tests, docs, commit and full-suite evidence therefore all stay inside this
  repo — `implement.py start <id>` from this checkout creates the worktree here
  and `wl` resolves this store, so no cross-store resolution is involved.
- **Explicit authorisation to edit `skill/`.** The repository-boundary rule
  forbids editing `skill/` unless explicitly instructed; this work item *is*
  that instruction, scoped to the files listed under **Key Files**.
- **Determinism preserved.** Tie-break stays `(sortIndex, id)`; no
  non-deterministic iteration order (sets are always sorted before use).
- **Narrow scope.** Do **not** change `wl dep` semantics, `sortIndex`
  generation/assignment, child classification, or the `parent` phase's broader
  control flow.
- **No new runtime dependencies;** Python 3.8+ compatible; stdlib only (as the
  existing module is).

## Existing state

`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`:

- `TERMINAL_STATUSES = {"in_review", "completed", "done", "deleted"}` (~line
  769), `_is_terminal_status()` (~772), `_is_terminal_child()` (~784, also
  treats a soft-deleted `deletedBy` child as terminal).
- `_classify_child()` (~810) — `skip-terminal` / `skip-in-progress` /
  `implement`.
- `_resolve_implementation_order(children, blockers)` (~836) — Kahn's
  algorithm; today:

  ```python
  for edge in blockers.get(cid, []):
      bid = str(edge.get("id", ""))
      if bid in child_ids:              # <-- terminal blockers still counted
          in_degree[cid] += 1
          dependents[bid].append(cid)
  ```

  The ready queue is `sorted(... in_degree[cid] == 0 ..., key=(sortIndex, id))`
  and is re-sorted after each release, so a terminal blocker with a high
  `sortIndex` delays its dependent.
- `_next_child_to_implement(children, blockers_map)` (~905) already gates on
  *non-terminal* in-chain blockers (`all(bid in terminal_ids ...)`), so the
  guard and the sort currently disagree — the inconsistency this item fixes.
- Caller `phase_parent` (~5124) calls `_resolve_implementation_order()` and
  returns early on a cycle error; `_next_child_to_implement()` then picks from
  the ordered list.
- Tests live in `skill/implement/tests/` (6 files, `.pi/test-config.json` group
  `implement` → `pytest -q skill/implement/tests/`); **no test currently covers
  `_resolve_implementation_order` or `_next_child_to_implement` directly.**

## Desired change

- Skip terminal blockers when building the graph in
  `_resolve_implementation_order()` — e.g.

  ```python
  if bid in child_ids and not _is_terminal_child(child_by_id[bid]):
      in_degree[cid] += 1
      dependents[bid].append(cid)
  ```

  (equivalently: collapse terminal children out of the graph before the sort).
  Terminal children remain present in the returned order so the caller still
  reports/finishes them, and their own placement is still decided by their own
  `(sortIndex, id)`.
- Cycle detection then operates over the non-terminal subgraph only; keep the
  same error message/format and the fail-fast return.
- Update the docstring (readiness rule + why terminal edges are excluded) and
  the ordering documentation in `skill/implement/SKILL.md`.
- Add the regression test module described in AC3.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (SorraAgents) — **Edit**:
  `_resolve_implementation_order()` graph construction + docstring;
  `_next_child_to_implement()` docstring cross-reference if needed.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_resolve_implementation_order.py` (SorraAgents) —
  **New**: ordering/readiness regression tests (AC3), including the red-then-
  green reproduction shape.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` (SorraAgents) — **Edit**: parent-recursion /
  dependency-order text states that terminal blockers do not gate readiness.
- `docs/dev/*` in SorraAgents — **Edit (if present)**: any ordering description
  that contradicts the new rule (verify with
  `grep -rn "topological\|dependency order" docs/ skill/implement/`).

## Risks and assumptions

**Risks**

- *Masking a real cycle.* Excluding terminal blockers from the graph could hide
  a cycle that passes through a terminal child. Mitigation: a cycle can only
  block work that still needs doing, so detection over the non-terminal
  subgraph is the correct semantics; document it in the docstring and cover it
  with AC3(f) (cycle among non-terminal children still fails fast).
- *Accidental behaviour drift elsewhere.* `_next_child_to_implement()` has its
  own terminal-aware guard; the fix must align with it rather than replace it.
  Mitigation: AC3(g) asserts the guard still refuses non-terminal-blocked
  children; AC4 forbids changing adjacent paths.
- *Cross-repo verification gap.* The AI_Hell audit/CI cannot see SorraAgents
  files, so a green AI_Hell report does not prove the fix. Mitigation: run the
  implement-skill pytest group and the SorraAgents full suite from the
  SorraAgents worktree and record the evidence (red/green, commit hash) on this
  item, per AH-0MUFGUYFC001A2OB.
- *Test-gate selection.* Changed-scope selection may not see the new test file
  until it is tracked; Mitigation: `git add` before the gate run and confirm the
  `implement` group is selected (otherwise fall back to full scope).
- *Scope creep.* The 2026-10-23 report also notes the confusing reported order
  generally and the manual `finish K0V4` step; richer ordering diagnostics or
  `parent`-phase rework are **not** in scope. Mitigation: record follow-ups as
  separate items (see Related work) rather than widening this fix.

**Assumptions**

- The item now lives in the **SorraAgents** worklog (relocated from AI_Hell by
  producer decision, per the SA-0MUWNKUIU007N876 precedent); the AI_Hell epic
  AH-0MV8BUKFK003Z23S remains recorded as the origin via `discovered-from`.
- Terminal blockers are pre-satisfied for *ordering* purposes but are still
  reported in the resolved order (existing `skip-terminal` classification
  handles them in the loop), so no caller contract changes.
- Soft-deleted children behave as terminal for this rule (they can never be
  implemented) — consistent with `_is_terminal_child()`.

## Related work

Cross-repo (SorraAgents — the code's owning repo; automated `find-related`
searched only the AI_Hell store because the item's prefix pins that store, and
its file matches are noise here):

- **SA-0MSQIJBTB008RHS1** — *completed* — V2: Dependency-graph resolution,
  topological ordering & cycle detection; the change that introduced
  `_resolve_implementation_order()`.
- **SA-0MSQBM2FK005NW1T** — *completed* — implement skill: `/skill:implement
  <parent-id>` must automatically implement children and blockers in the chain;
  defined the in-chain/external blocker split and the blocked-child guard.
- **SA-0MUWNKUIU007N876** — *open* — implement.py parent ignores the
  do-not-delegate tag when selecting the next child; same selection path
  (`_next_child_to_implement`), different rule. **Relocated** from the AI_Hell
  worklog because `implement.py` is SorraAgents-owned — the precedent for the
  OPEN QUESTION below.
- **SA-0MUWNHKQH0034DW9** — *completed* — implement skill: drive all epic
  children to completion (fresh session per child); the `parent`/`drive` flow
  that consumes this ordering.

AI_Hell (origin store — historical, retained for traceability after the relocation):

- **AH-0MV8BUKFK003Z23S** — Create an improved Phase Shift effect — the epic
  whose run exposed the defect (`discovered-from`).
- **AH-0MUFGUYFC001A2OB** — ship skill kebab-case fix — *completed* — the
  cross-repo precedent: AI_Hell item, SorraAgents commit, cross-repo evidence
  recorded on the item.
- **AH-0MTXLWCWO005OSCZ** — run-release Discord notification wiring — the
  earlier cross-repo precedent referenced by the above.
- **AH-0MVFBCVIS007BN81** — implement.py: behind-only child worktree
  mis-detected as "has changes" and auto-finished — *open* — sibling defect in
  the same `parent`/`finish` machinery (no fix overlap).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interactive interview round was held: the seed context (problem statement,
observed impact, expected behaviour, suggested fix and ACs) was sufficient to
draft an actionable brief, and the repo research below answered the remaining
implementation questions.

- **Q1 — Which repository owns the code, and where does the fix land?**
  — Answer (repo research + precedent, not a producer question):
  **SorraAgents**. `~/.pi/agent/skills` is a symlink to
  `SorraAgents/skill`; the AI_Hell checkout has no `skill/` tree
  (`find / -name implement.py` → `SorraAgents/skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`,
  identical to the installed copy, `diff` clean). Precedent
  **AH-0MUFGUYFC001A2OB** (AI_Hell item, commit `4be04fa7a` on SorraAgents
  `dev`, cross-repo evidence in a comment) and **AH-0MTXLWCWO005OSCZ**. Source:
  `git log --grep="AH-"` in SorraAgents; comment on AH-0MUFGUYFC001A2OB.
- **Q2 — Does `implement.py` work at all against a foreign worklog store?**
  — Answer (repo research): yes. `implement.py` routes every `wl` call through
  `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.resolve_worklog_flags()`, whose
  prefix-to-sibling scan maps an `AH-…` id to `AI_Hell/.worklog` even when cwd
  is SorraAgents, so `implement.py start AH-0MVL5B7C80000MT6` from the SorraAgents
  checkout yields a SorraAgents worktree + AI_Hell worklog. Source:
  `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` (~lines 290–370).
- **Q3 — How should terminal be defined for the readiness rule?**
  — Answer (repo research): reuse `_is_terminal_child()` (statuses
  `in_review`/`completed`/`done`/`deleted` plus soft-deleted), matching the
  guard already used by `_next_child_to_implement()`. Source:
  `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (~769–808, ~905–955).
- **Q4 — Is there an existing test to extend?**
  — Answer (repo research): no. `skill/implement/tests/` has 6 modules and none

  (`grep -rn` clean), so AC3 creates a new module covered by the existing
  `.pi/test-config.json` `implement` group. Source: repo inspection.
- **Q5 — Should this item be relocated to the SorraAgents worklog?**
  — Answer (producer, interactive reply): **yes — recreate it on
  `../SorraAgents`, `wl sync`, and delete the AI_Hell item when done.**
  Rationale/precedent: `implement.py` is agent-infrastructure code owned by

### Goal

Extend the in-repo, fail-open Herdr CLI helper with a session-level pane/agent
boundary and provide a deterministic recording **fake** Herdr CLI, so the pane
transport and its tests can exercise `pane split` / `agent start` /
`agent prompt` / `agent wait` / `pane close` without a live Herdr.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Pane-per-child in the caller's tab.** For each startable child, drive runs `pane split` (no `tab create`/`workspace create`) with `--cwd`, started via `agent start` and prompted via `agent prompt --wait`; asserted by a fake-CLI test.
- A recording fake Herdr CLI (test-only shim plus in-process runner with scripted responses) lets tests assert exact herdr invocations (arguments and order) and simulate `done`, `blocked`, `timeout`, `agent_not_ready` and CLI-failure transitions with no live Herdr.
- Agent names `drive-<child-id-lowercased>` are validated against herdr's `[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}` rule with deterministic truncation; unit tests cover valid, truncated and collision cases.
- `agent start` requiring an interactive shell prompt is handled: `agent_not_ready` is retried within the configured wait budget or surfaced as a reported reason — never a crash.
- **Build, tests, and full suite.** Changed-scope tests pass before commit; the dev-push full-suite gate is green.

## Implementation notes

- **Forked-decision resolution (intake Appendix):** keep the boundary in
  `skill/shared/` and reuse `herdr_pane.py`'s `HERDR_BIN_PATH` resolution,
  subprocess env handling and fail-open return style — do not duplicate that
  logic. Additive changes only to in-repo files; no edits to repo-external
  herdr skill or `~/.pi/agent/extensions/`.
- Surface (one injectable client, every call returning a parsed result or a
  fail-open `{"success": false, "reason": ...}`, never raising):
  `pane split --current --cwd <path> [--env K=V] [--focus|--no-focus]`,
  `agent start <name> --kind pi --pane <id> -- --approve --no-extensions`,
  `agent prompt <target> <text> --wait [--until] [--timeout]`,
  `agent wait <name> --until done|blocked`, `pane close <id>`,
  `pane rename <id> <label>`.
- Parse ids defensively from `.result.pane.pane_id` and agent JSON; treat
  unknown shapes as a reported failure (Herdr API-drift mitigation).
- Fake CLI lives under the tests tree (`skill/shared/tests/`), scripted by the
  test, emitting JSON matching the real CLI shape.

**Key Files:**
- `skill/shared/herdr_pane.py`
- `skill/shared/herdr_session.py` (new, if split out)
- `skill/shared/tests/fake_herdr_cli.py` (new)
- `skill/shared/tests/test_herdr_session.py` (new)
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`

## Dependencies

None — foundation slice; blocks the spawner and lifecycle slices.

## Deliverables

- Session-level Herdr boundary helper (split/agent start/prompt/wait/close,
  rename) reusing `herdr_pane.py` conventions.
- Recording fake Herdr CLI + fixtures.
- Unit tests, all green, no live Herdr needed.
- Short reference-doc note for the helper.

### Goal

Add `_pane_session_spawner` next to `_default_session_spawner` and select the
transport per invocation: pane driving only when Herdr is detected **and** the
operator opted in; otherwise the existing headless `pi -p` spawner is used
unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Pane-per-child in the caller's tab.** For each startable child, drive runs `pane split` with `--cwd` (no tab create), then `agent prompt`; asserted by a fake-CLI test.
- **Opt-in with fail-open fallback.** Pane driving activates only when `HERDR_ENV=1`, a resolvable herdr binary and `--pane-sessions`/`IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_PANE_SESSIONS=1` agree; tests cover absent and opt-in.
- **Environment isolation is preserved for pane children.** The child process receives `IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_ACTIVE=1` and `IMPLEMENT_WORKTREE_PATH` without `PI_SESSION_ID`/`PI_SESSION_FILE`; `pane split --env` args are asserted.
- **Focus behaviour.** Default is `--no-focus` so the caller's focus is unchanged; `--focus` switches to each new child pane and the flag passed to `pane split` is asserted.
- `_pane_session_spawner` returns the `_default_session_spawner` result shape plus `pane_id` and `transport`, so existing `phase_drive` success handling is unchanged.
- **Build, tests, and full suite.** Changed-scope tests pass before commit; the dev-push full-suite gate is green.

## Implementation notes

- `_pane_session_spawner(child_id, worktree_path, timeout, env,
  verbose=False)` → `{"success", "returncode", "reason", "pane_id",
  "transport"}`.
- Selection: `spawner = spawn_session or _select_session_spawner(...)`,
  keeping the existing `spawn_session` test-injection point. Detect with
  `HERDR_ENV=1` plus herdr-binary resolution (reuse the shared resolver);
  opt in via `--pane-sessions` or `IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_PANE_SESSIONS=1`.
- New argparse flags: `--pane-sessions` / `--no-pane-sessions` (default:
  env-driven) and `--focus` / `--no-focus` (default `--no-focus`), threaded
  into `phase_drive`.
- Child env comes from the existing `_child_session_env`; the pane transport
  passes it as `pane split --env` pairs, and the TUI launch uses an
  `env -u PI_SESSION_ID -u PI_SESSION_FILE` prefix so the driving session's
  identity never leaks into the pane.
- Do **not** change `_default_session_spawner`: headless `pi -p` stays the
  default outside Herdr for the downtime worker, audit dispatch and CI.

**Key Files:**
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`
- `skill/implement/tests/test_drive_child_session.py`
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` (Step 6.1)

## Deliverables

- `_pane_session_spawner`, transport selection, CLI flags.
- Env-isolation and focus handling.
- Unit tests: detection matrix (herdr-absent / opt-out / opt-in), split/start/

### Goal

Drive the pane-side lifecycle to completion in `phase_drive`: wait on session
state (never process exit), report blocked children, bound the wait with the
existing timeouts, and close or explicitly retain every pane — with additive
report parity for human and `--json` output.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Driver waits on session state, not process exit.** Completion of a child is decided by `agent wait --until done|blocked` plus the `phase_parent` stage re-read; tests cover done, blocked, timeout.
- **Blocked children are reported, not silently abandoned.** When an agent reports `blocked`, drive stops, records `blocked_child`/`blocked_pane`, leaves the pane open and names it.
- **No orphaned sessions:** a pane created by drive is either (a) closed once its child reaches a terminal stage or (b) retained and reported; tests assert close per success and no close when blocked.
- **Timeouts and iteration bounds are enforced across the new transport.** `IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_CHILD_TIMEOUT` and `--max-child-sessions` still bound the wait; a timeout closes the pane and stops the chain.
- **Report parity.** Human and `--json` reports keep the existing shape and gain `pane_id` per driven child plus `transport`; the summary lists retained panes, asserted by tests.
- **Build, tests, and full suite.** Changed-scope tests pass before commit; the dev-push full-suite gate is green.

## Implementation notes

- `phase_parent` stays the authority for terminality; the `agent wait` result
  is only a fast-path/stop signal. Reuse `_reconcile_spawn_failure` so a child
  that reached a terminal stage before the wait expired is still reported as
  `completed-late`, not failed.
- `blocked` → report keys `blocked_child` / `blocked_pane`, a `retained_panes`
  entry, and an actionable message naming the pane (e.g.
  `herdr pane read <pane_id>`); title the pane via
  `herdr_pane.update_pane_title(status, pane_id=...)` (`⚠️`/`🚫` verdicts).
- Close path: `pane close <id>` after the child's terminal stage is confirmed;
  retain on blocked/failed with a verdict title. Never leak silently.
- `_emit_phase_report` gains additive keys only; the human rendering appends a
  "panes retained for inspection" list. Existing deterministic orchestration
  tests (`ScriptedParent` / `RecordingSpawner`) keep passing unchanged.
- Timeout behaviour keeps today's semantics: close the pane, record `reason`,
  stop the chain (reconciled against the child's real stage first).

**Key Files:**
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (`phase_drive`, `_emit_phase_report`)
- `tests/test_implement_drive.py`
- `skill/implement/tests/test_drive_child_session.py`
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` (Step 6.1)

## Dependencies

- Pane session spawner and opt-in transport selection.

## Deliverables

- done / blocked / timeout lifecycle handling with `phase_parent` authority.
- Close-or-retain rule with pane-title verdicts.
- Report fields (`pane_id`, `transport`, blocked/retained panes) plus human
  rendering, with parity tests.
- Doc updates for blocked-child handling and retained panes.

## Goal

Replace the whole-directory `node_modules` symlink in `implement.py start` with a **worktree-local link farm** so workspace packages resolve to the worktree's own source tree. Parent: SA-0MVMZBJGT00718ZO.

## Problem (parent: SA-0MVMZBJGT00718ZO)

`_ensure_node_modules_symlink` (~L1695 in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`) symlinks `<worktree>/node_modules -> <main-checkout>/node_modules`. When the main checkout's `node_modules/@worklog/shared` is a relative symlink `../../packages/shared`, every `@worklog/shared` import in the worktree resolves to the **main checkout's** `packages/shared/dist` (gitignored, built by `npm run build` in whichever checkout ran it last) — the worktree's own `packages/shared/src/**` changes are invisible to the build/test gate (false red, false green).

## Desired change (producer-decided: link farm)

Replace `_ensure_node_modules_symlink` with an idempotent link-farm creator:

- Create a **real** `<worktree>/node_modules` directory containing one symlink per main-checkout `node_modules` entry, recursing into scoped packages (`@worklog/*`, `@types/*`, …), and linking `.bin` as a whole directory.
- Override workspace packages (e.g. `@worklog/shared`) to the worktree's own `packages/*` — resolved relative to the worktree via the `workspaces` field or a small allow-list; keep the mechanism workspace-aware, not hard-coded to `@worklog/shared`.
- Keep `_ensure_nested_node_modules_symlinks` (OSL-0MUFG3PJA00379CT) unchanged and working.
- Add a resolution check: `@worklog/shared`'s resolved package root must equal `<worktree>/packages/shared`; expose it in the `start` JSON report.
- Idempotent and refreshable: re-running re-materialises entries when the main checkout's dependency set changes. Documented refresh = re-run of the link step (or `implement.py start`) from the main checkout.
- No writes through the farm into the main checkout's `node_modules`/`dist`; `npm install` inside a worktree stays forbidden (AC5); automated `rsync` of worktree `dist` into the main checkout is rejected.
- Best-effort/non-fatal on tooling edge cases (Windows junctions per ContextHub `link-shared.mjs` precedent); degrade to the old whole-dir symlink behaviour for repos without a workspace shared package.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `implement.py start` outputs a real-directory link farm at `<worktree>/node_modules` (per-entry symlinks, scoped recursion, `.bin` whole-link) instead of a whole-directory symlink, with `@worklog/shared` resolving (`os.path.realpath`) to `<worktree>/packages/shared`.
2. The `start` JSON report includes the resolution-check result key (e.g. `shared_resolution_ok: true`, with the resolved root), present on both fresh `start` and refresh.
3. The step is idempotent (re-run creates no duplicates) and refreshable when the main checkout's dependency set changes; verified by automated tests from the F1 test-first item.
4. No writes pass through the farm into the main checkout's `node_modules`; the main checkout stays git-clean of everything except gitignored build artefacts after start → build → gate → finish.
5. Repos without a workspace shared package keep the previous whole-directory symlink behaviour (degradation path, tested); the nested/workspace `node_modules` mirroring (OSL-0MUFG3PJA00379CT) keeps working.

## Goal

Make `implement.py finish` **fail closed** when a worktree changes `packages/shared/src/**` while `@worklog/shared` still resolves to the main checkout's stale `dist` — an actionable error naming the stale path and remediation, so a green gate never silently passes on the wrong code. Parent: SA-0MVMZBJGT00718ZO.

## Problem (parent: SA-0MVMZBJGT00718ZO)

`phase_finish` runs build → test gate → commit from the worktree. If resolution is stale (worktree's `@worklog/shared` → main checkout's `packages/shared/dist`), the gate either false-reds on correct new code (WL-0MVK6S4HM005GBCO) or false-greens on broken code. The gate currently cannot distinguish "shared code changed in this worktree" from "shared code unchanged" and exposes no resolution diagnostic.

## Desired change (producer-decided: hard-fail)

1. Extract the resolution check from the F2 link-farm feature into a shared helper (`@worklog/shared` resolved package root == `<worktree>/packages/shared`), reused by the `start` JSON report and `finish`.
2. In `phase_finish`, before the test gate (after the build step), compute whether the worktree diff touches `packages/shared/src/**` and whether the resolution check fails; when both hold, hard-fail with a message naming the stale `<main-checkout>/packages/shared/dist` path and the remediation (re-run `implement.py start` / the documented refresh command from the main checkout, then rebuild).
3. End-to-end probe verification (AC1): in a fresh worktree, a probe change under `packages/shared/src/**` is observed by the sanctioned gate (`run_tests.py --type full --scope full`), and an unmodified main checkout would not observe it.
4. Detection no-ops for repos without a workspace shared package (degradation path).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `finish` hard-fails (non-zero, no commit, item released to `open` with the failure comment) with an actionable message naming the stale `<main-checkout>/packages/shared/dist` path and the remediation when the worktree diff touches `packages/shared/src/**` AND the resolution check fails — covered by the F1 negative-path test.
2. The gate passes normally when the resolution check succeeds (worktree-local link farm present), including when shared source is unchanged.
3. The e2e probe proves the worktree's `packages/shared/src/**` change is observed by the gate (`run_tests.py --type full --scope full`) from inside a fresh worktree, and that an unmodified main checkout does not observe it.
4. The resolution helper is shared between `start` and `finish` (single source of truth), and its detection logic is covered by the F1 unit tests.
5. No change to main-checkout build/test behaviour (byte-for-byte unchanged outside worktree setups); the main checkout stays git-clean of non-gitignored artefacts after start → build → gate → finish.

## Goal

If the Lane A clean-room measurement (sibling child) records a valid run **above** the 600 s total LLM wall-clock gate, land the smallest **model-throughput lever** that makes the committed gate green: route the whole single-item audit path — including the `false-positive-screen` call and Phase 2 deep analysis — onto a documented fast model through an explicit, opt-in surface, keeping the full-model fallback semantics and the frozen verdict contract.

Blocked by / conditional on the Lane A child: this item **starts only when the Lane A re-measurement records a valid run exceeding 600 s**. If Lane A meets the gate, close this item as not-needed citing the Lane A evidence (no code change).

Parent: SA-0MVKXNWRS005EKBM. Existing surface today: `--phase1-model` / `AUDIT_PHASE1_MODEL` (`_resolve_phase1_model`) routes **only** the Phase 1 screen, which for a single item is one call out of three (~576 s of ~1539 s) — not enough on its own; the `false-positive-screen` call and `phase2_deep` stay on `DEFAULT_MODEL` (`Local Proxy/plan`).

## Scope

1. Generalise the fast-model surface so a single-item audit can route **all** of its LLM calls to a fast alias — either by extending `--phase1-model`/`AUDIT_PHASE1_MODEL` to the whole single-item path (documented semantics), or by adding an explicit `--fast-model` / `AUDIT_FAST_MODEL` surface (prefer the smallest surface that stays opt-in and does not change any default invocation).
2. Route the `false-positive-screen` call site (`_run_false_positive_screen`) through the resolved fast model, preserving the existing full-model fallback when the fast model's output is unparseable.
3. Route `phase2_deep` for a single-item run through the fast model when the surface is enabled, with the same fallback.
4. Keep every default unchanged: with no flag/env, the resolved audit model is used exactly as today.
5. Re-measure the single-item audit with the lever enabled, on the same small-item shape and the same clean-room conditions as Lane A, and record the before/after table in `docs/dev/audit-performance-baseline.md`.

## Non-goals (frozen by the parent)

- No change to `met`/`unmet`/`partial`/`adjusted` semantics, to the ready-to-close gate, or to when `partial` degradation happens.
- No timeout raise to mask cost.
- No remote (non-local-proxy) model routing — out of scope unless the producer explicitly authorises it.
- Saturation guard: only 2 local proxy slots exist; fast-model routing must not spawn additional concurrent calls (call count may only stay equal or decrease).

## Test-first ordering

Write the failing tests first (routed-model selection, fallback, parity, default-unchanged), then implement the routing, then re-measure and update the docs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- With no flag and no environment variable set, a single-item audit resolves exactly the same models for `false-positive-screen`, `parent` and `phase2_deep` as before this change (regression test proves the default is unchanged).
- Any lever that lands is covered by tests: unit tests prove the routed model selection for the `false-positive-screen`, Phase 1 and Phase 2 deep calls and its full-model fallback on unparseable output without changing `met`/`unmet`/`partial`/`adjusted` outcomes on a fixed item fixture, so an unparseable fast-model response is retried once on the full model before degrading to `partial`.
- A clean-room re-measurement with the lever enabled is recorded in `docs/dev/audit-performance-baseline.md` as a before/after table (baseline: the Lane A figures) with command, model served, slot-query status, ceiling source and per-call profile, and the total LLM wall clock is reported against the unchanged ≤ 600 s gate.
- If the ≤ 600 s target cannot be met on the current model, a model-throughput lever lands first: fast-model routing via the existing `--phase1-model` / `AUDIT_PHASE1_MODEL` surface, extended to the whole single-item path as needed, lands before any call-count lever (Lane C) is attempted, and the lever-enabled re-measurement is recorded.
- Verdict semantics and the ready-to-close gate stay frozen and the ≤ 10 min gate is not weakened: the existing `met`/`unmet`/`partial`/`adjusted` and ready-to-close tests pass unchanged, a `partial` fallback never degrades to `met`, and no timeout is raised.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `skill/audit/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`, and `docs/dev/audit-performance-baseline.md` — covering the generalised model surface (precedence, defaults, fallback-on-unparseable behaviour, opt-in default).
- Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Opt-in only: no default invocation changes behaviour or model.
- Verdict semantics and the ready-to-close gate stay frozen; the ≤ 10 min gate is not weakened.
- Runner remains `[READ-ONLY AUDIT]` apart from the documented persistence, lifecycle and ruff-remediation exceptions.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_phase1_model.py` — extend for the generalised surface and default-unchanged regression
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_false_positive.py` — false-positive-screen routing/fallback
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_phase2.py` — phase-2 deep routing/fallback and verdict parity

1. Fold the false-positive classification into the Phase 1 parent screen call (one call performs both jobs for a single-item run), or otherwise collapse the 3 serial calls to ≤ 2 — whichever is the smallest change that keeps the prompt contracts parseable.
